paragraphs.text: In the mean time, when the many thousands of the multitude were gathered together, insomuch that they trod one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων.
paragraphs.translit: En hois episynachtheisōn tōn myriadōn tou ochlou, hōste katapatein allēlous, ērxato legein pros tous mathētas autou prōton· Prosechete heautois apo tēs zymēs, hētis estin hypokrisis, tōn Pharisaiōn.

paragraphs.text: But there is nothing covered up, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ouden de synkekalymmenon estin ho ouk apokalyphthēsetai, kai krypton ho ou gnōsthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore whatsoever ye have said in the darkness shall be heard in the light; and what ye have spoken in the ear in the inner chambers shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.
paragraphs.original: ἀνθʼ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
paragraphs.translit: anthʼ hōn hosa en tē skotia eipate en tō phōti akousthēsetai, kai ho pros to ous elalēsate en tois tameiois kērychthēsetai epi tōn dōmatōn.

paragraphs.text: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
paragraphs.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Legō de hymin tois philois mou, mē phobēthēte apo tōn apokteinontōn to sōma kai meta tauta mē echontōn perissoteron ti poiēsai.

paragraphs.text: But I will warn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, who after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.
paragraphs.original: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ἐμβαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.
paragraphs.translit: hypodeixō de hymin tina phobēthēte· phobēthēte ton meta to apokteinai echonta exousian embalein eis tēn geennan· nai, legō hymin, touton phobēthēte.

paragraphs.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pence? and not one of them is forgotten in the sight of God.
paragraphs.original: οὐχὶ πέντε στρουθία πωλοῦνται ἀσσαρίων δύο; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπιλελησμένον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ouchi pente strouthia pōlountai assariōn dyo; kai hen ex autōn ouk estin epilelēsmenon enōpion tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν πᾶσαι ἠρίθμηνται· μὴ φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε.
paragraphs.translit: alla kai hai triches tēs kephalēs hymōn pasai ērithmēntai· mē phobeisthe· pollōn strouthiōn diapherete.

paragraphs.text: And I say unto you, Every one who shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:
paragraphs.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Legō de hymin, pas hos an homologēsē en emoi emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, kai ho hyios tou anthrōpou homologēsei en autō emprosthen tōn angelōn tou theou·

paragraphs.text: but he that denieth me in the presence of men shall be denied in the presence of the angels of God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de arnēsamenos me enōpion tōn anthrōpōn aparnēthēsetai enōpion tōn angelōn tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And every one who shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Spirit it shall not be forgiven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas hos erei logon eis ton hyion tou anthrōpou, aphethēsetai autō tō de eis to hagion pneuma blasphēmēsanti ouk aphethēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And when they bring you before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious how or what ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·
paragraphs.translit: hotan de eispherōsin hymas epi tas synagōgas kai tas archas kai tas exousias, mē merimnēsēte pōs ē ti apologēsēsthe ē ti eipēte·

paragraphs.text: for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that very hour what ye ought to say.
paragraphs.original: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: to gar hagion pneuma didaxei hymas en autē tē hōra ha dei eipein.

paragraphs.text: And one out of the multitude said unto him, Teacher, bid my brother divide the inheritance with me.
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de tis ek tou ochlou autō· Didaskale, eipe tō adelphō mou merisasthai metʼ emou tēn klēronomian.

paragraphs.text: But he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autō· Anthrōpe, tis me katestēsen kritēn ē meristēn ephʼ hymas;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Take heed, and keep yourselves from all covetousness: for a man`s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros autous· Horate kai phylassesthe apo pasēs pleonexias, hoti ouk en tō perisseuein tini hē zōē autou estin ek tōn hyparchontōn autō.

paragraphs.text: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de parabolēn pros autous legōn· Anthrōpou tinos plousiou euphorēsen hē chōra.

paragraphs.text: and he reasoned within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not where to bestow my fruits?
paragraphs.original: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;
paragraphs.translit: kai dielogizeto en heautō legōn· Ti poiēsō, hoti ouk echō pou synaxō tous karpous mou;

paragraphs.text: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my grain and my goods.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Touto poiēsō· kathelō mou tas apothēkas kai meizonas oikodomēsō, kai synaxō ekei panta ton siton kai ta agatha mou,

paragraphs.text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, be merry.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai erō tē psychē mou· Psychē, echeis polla agatha keimena eis etē polla· anapauou, phage, pie, euphrainou.

paragraphs.text: But God said unto him, Thou foolish one, this night is thy soul required of thee; and the things which thou hast prepared, whose shall they be?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autō ho theos· Aphrōn, tautē tē nykti tēn psychēn sou apaitousin apo sou· ha de hētoimasas, tini estai;

paragraphs.text: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs ho thēsaurizōn heautō kai mē eis theon ploutōn.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for [your] life, what ye shall eat; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on.
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathētas autou· Dia touto legō hymin, mē merimnate tē psychē ti phagēte, mēde tō sōmati ti endysēsthe.

paragraphs.text: For the life is more than the food, and the body than the raiment.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.
paragraphs.translit: hē gar psychē pleion estin tēs trophēs kai to sōma tou endymatos.

paragraphs.text: Consider the ravens, that they sow not, neither reap; which have no store-chamber nor barn; and God feedeth them: of how much more value are ye than the birds!
paragraphs.original: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.
paragraphs.translit: katanoēsate tous korakas hoti ou speirousin oude therizousin, hois ouk estin tameion oude apothēkē, kai ho theos trephei autous· posō mallon hymeis diapherete tōn peteinōn.

paragraphs.text: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit unto the measure of his life?
paragraphs.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;
paragraphs.translit: tis de ex hymōn merimnōn dynatai epi tēn hēlikian autou prostheinai pēchyn;

paragraphs.text: If then ye are not able to do even that which is least, why are ye anxious concerning the rest?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;
paragraphs.translit: ei oun oude elachiston dynasthe, ti peri tōn loipōn merimnate;

paragraphs.text: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they toil not, neither do they spin; yet I say unto you, Even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
paragraphs.original: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει· οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: katanoēsate ta krina pōs auxanei· ou kopia oude nēthei· legō de hymin, oude Solomōn en pasē tē doxē autou periebaleto hōs hen toutōn.

paragraphs.text: But if God doth so clothe the grass in the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven; how much more [shall he clothe] you, O ye of little faith?
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέζει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.
paragraphs.translit: ei de en agrō ton chorton onta sēmeron kai aurion eis klibanon ballomenon ho theos houtōs amphiezei, posō mallon hymas, oligopistoi.

paragraphs.text: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, and what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,
paragraphs.translit: kai hymeis mē zēteite ti phagēte kai ti piēte, kai mē meteōrizesthe,

paragraphs.text: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: but your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: tauta gar panta ta ethnē tou kosmou epizētousin, hymōn de ho patēr oiden hoti chrēzete toutōn.

paragraphs.text: Yet seek ye his kingdom, and these things shall be added unto you.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: plēn zēteite tēn basileian autou, kai tauta prostethēsetai hymin.

paragraphs.text: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father`s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.
paragraphs.translit: Mē phobou, to mikron poimnion, hoti eudokēsen ho patēr hymōn dounai hymin tēn basileian.

paragraphs.text: Sell that which ye have, and give alms; make for yourselves purses which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief draweth near, neither moth destroyeth.
paragraphs.original: πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην· ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα, θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει·
paragraphs.translit: pōlēsate ta hyparchonta hymōn kai dote eleēmosynēn· poiēsate heautois ballantia mē palaioumena, thēsauron anekleipton en tois ouranois, hopou kleptēs ouk engizei oude sēs diaphtheirei·

paragraphs.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται.
paragraphs.translit: hopou gar estin ho thēsauros hymōn, ekei kai hē kardia hymōn estai.

paragraphs.text: Let your loins be girded about, and your lamps burning;
paragraphs.original: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,
paragraphs.translit: Estōsan hymōn hai osphyes periezōsmenai kai hoi lychnoi kaiomenoi,

paragraphs.text: and be ye yourselves like unto men looking for their lord, when he shall return from the marriage feast; that, when he cometh and knocketh, they may straightway open unto him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hymeis homoioi anthrōpois prosdechomenois ton kyrion heautōn pote analysē ek tōn gamōn, hina elthontos kai krousantos eutheōs anoixōsin autō.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them sit down to meat, and shall come and serve them.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi douloi ekeinoi, hous elthōn ho kyrios heurēsei grēgorountas· amēn legō hymin hoti perizōsetai kai anaklinei autous kai parelthōn diakonēsei autois.

paragraphs.text: And if he shall come in the second watch, and if in the third, and find [them] so blessed are those [servants].
paragraphs.original: κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.
paragraphs.translit: kan en tē deutera kan en tē tritē phylakē elthē kai heurē houtōs, makarioi eisin ekeinoi.

paragraphs.text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not have left his house to be broken through.
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Touto de ginōskete hoti ei ēdei ho oikodespotēs poia hōra ho kleptēs erchetai, ouk an aphēken diorychthēnai ton oikon autou.

paragraphs.text: Be ye also ready: for in an hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai hymeis ginesthe hetoimoi, hoti hē hōra ou dokeite ho hyios tou anthrōpou erchetai.

paragraphs.text: And Peter said, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even unto all?
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de ho Petros· Kyrie, pros hēmas tēn parabolēn tautēn legeis ē kai pros pantas;

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said, Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall set over his household, to give them their portion of food in due season?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen ho kyrios· Tis ara estin ho pistos oikonomos, ho phronimos, hon katastēsei ho kyrios epi tēs therapeias autou tou didonai en kairō to sitometrion;

paragraphs.text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.
paragraphs.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·
paragraphs.translit: makarios ho doulos ekeinos, hon elthōn ho kyrios autou heurēsei poiounta houtōs·

paragraphs.text: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will set him over all that he hath.
paragraphs.original: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: alēthōs legō hymin hoti epi pasin tois hyparchousin autou katastēsei auton.

paragraphs.text: But if that servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,
paragraphs.translit: ean de eipē ho doulos ekeinos en tē kardia autou· Chronizei ho kyrios mou erchesthai, kai arxētai typtein tous paidas kai tas paidiskas, esthiein te kai pinein kai methyskesthai,

paragraphs.text: the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he expecteth not, and in an hour when he knoweth not, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with the unfaithful.
paragraphs.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.
paragraphs.translit: hēxei ho kyrios tou doulou ekeinou en hēmera hē ou prosdoka kai en hōra hē ou ginōskei, kai dichotomēsei auton kai to meros autou meta tōn apistōn thēsei.

paragraphs.text: And that servant, who knew his lord`s will, and made not ready, nor did according to his will, shall be beaten with many [stripes];
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·
paragraphs.translit: ekeinos de ho doulos ho gnous to thelēma tou kyriou autou kai mē hetoimasas ē poiēsas pros to thelēma autou darēsetai pollas·

paragraphs.text: but he that knew not, and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few [stripes]. And to whomsoever much is given, of him shall much be required: and to whom they commit much, of him will they ask the more.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de mē gnous poiēsas de axia plēgōn darēsetai oligas. panti de hō edothē poly, poly zētēthēsetai parʼ autou, kai hō parethento poly, perissoteron aitēsousin auton.

paragraphs.text: I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire, if it is already kindled?
paragraphs.original: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;
paragraphs.translit: Pyr ēlthon balein epi tēn gēn, kai ti thelō ei ēdē anēphthē;

paragraphs.text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!
paragraphs.original: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: baptisma de echō baptisthēnai, kai pōs synechomai heōs hotou telesthē.

paragraphs.text: Think ye that I am come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:
paragraphs.original: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἢ διαμερισμόν.
paragraphs.translit: dokeite hoti eirēnēn paregenomēn dounai en tē gē; ouchi, legō hymin, allʼ ē diamerismon.

paragraphs.text: for there shall be from henceforth five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
paragraphs.original: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,
paragraphs.translit: esontai gar apo tou nyn pente en heni oikō diamemerismenoi, treis epi dysin kai dyo epi trisin,

paragraphs.text: They shall be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother in law against her daughter in law, and daughter in law against her mother in law.
paragraphs.original: διαμερισθήσονται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν.
paragraphs.translit: diameristhēsontai patēr epi hyiō kai hyios epi patri, mētēr epi thygatera kai thygatēr epi tēn mētera, penthera epi tēn nymphēn autēs kai nymphē epi tēn pentheran.

paragraphs.text: And he said to the multitudes also, When ye see a cloud rising in the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it cometh to pass.
paragraphs.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ἴδητε νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·
paragraphs.translit: Elegen de kai tois ochlois· Hotan idēte nephelēn anatellousan epi dysmōn, eutheōs legete hoti Ombros erchetai, kai ginetai houtōs·

paragraphs.text: And when [ye see] a south wind blowing, ye say, There will be a scorching heat; and it cometh to pass.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai hotan noton pneonta, legete hoti Kausōn estai, kai ginetai.

paragraphs.text: Ye hypocrites, ye know how to interpret the face of the earth and the heaven; but how is it that ye know not how to interpret this time?
paragraphs.original: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν δὲ καιρὸν τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν;
paragraphs.translit: hypokritai, to prosōpon tēs gēs kai tou ouranou oidate dokimazein, ton de kairon touton pōs ouk oidate dokimazein;

paragraphs.text: And why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?
paragraphs.original: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;
paragraphs.translit: Ti de kai aphʼ heautōn ou krinete to dikaion;

paragraphs.text: For as thou art going with thine adversary before the magistrate, on the way give diligence to be quit of him; lest haply he drag thee unto the judge, and the judge shall deliver thee to the officer, and the officer shall cast thee into prison.
paragraphs.original: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπʼ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτής σε παραδώσει τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs gar hypageis meta tou antidikou sou epʼ archonta, en tē hodō dos ergasian apēllachthai apʼ autou, mēpote katasyrē se pros ton kritēn, kai ho kritēs se paradōsei tō praktori, kai ho praktōr se balei eis phylakēn.

paragraphs.text: I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the very last mite.
paragraphs.original: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.
paragraphs.translit: legō soi, ou mē exelthēs ekeithen heōs kai to eschaton lepton apodōs.
